The Production Floor Visibility Gap

In most factories, supervision relies on physical walk-arounds and end-of-shift reports. The gap between a process deviation and corrective action is measured in hours — not seconds.

≥15 min
Average detection latency

Time from a process deviation to a supervisor's awareness — often discovered only at end-of-shift audit.

≈30%
Productivity loss

Operators idle, repeating steps, or performing out-of-sequence actions without contextual, real-time guidance.

100%
Cameras already installed

RTSP/ONVIF streams exist — the data is there. What's missing is intelligence extracting meaning from it in real time.

Research Hypothesis

Frozen visual foundation models (V-JEPA 2, DINOv2) can serve as generalizable feature extractors for industrial Human Action Recognition (HAR), enabling lightweight task-specific classifiers that run on edge hardware — closing the loop between visual data and real-time operational insight.

Transfer learning — frozen backbone Subject-aware generalization Edge deployment target Industria 4.0 feedback loop

02
Frozen Embedding Extraction 02_Embedding_Extraction.ipynb

Extracts 1024-dim embeddings from two frozen vision transformers. Per clip: sample 16 frames → YOLOv8 top-down crop → frozen backbone → temporal pooling → .npz. No backbone gradients — pure feature extraction.

V-JEPA 2
facebook/vjepa2-vitl-fpc64-256
Masked joint embedding prediction across video patches. Learns temporal consistency — predicts representations of masked spatiotemporal regions from context. 64 frames × 256px, ViT-L backbone.
embeddings.npz — 3,423 × 1024
DINOv2 (winner)
facebook/dinov2-large (ViT-L/14)
Self-supervised ViT with knowledge distillation on curated imagery. Dense spatial features via [CLS] token. Applied per-frame on YOLO crop, then averaged across the 16-frame window. Patch 14×14, output 1024-dim.
embeddings_dinov2.npz — 3,425 × 1024
03
MLP Head Training 03_Train_HAR_Head.ipynb

Trains a lightweight MLP classifier on frozen embeddings using three simultaneous anti-imbalance strategies. Subject-aware split prevents any subject from appearing in both train and val — ensuring generalization to unseen operators.

# MLP Architecture Input: 1024-dim embedding → Linear(1024, 512) → BatchNorm + ReLU + Dropout(0.3) → Linear(512, 256) → BatchNorm + ReLU + Dropout(0.3) → Linear(256, 12) → Softmax (inference)
# Training Config epochs: 100 batch_size: 64 · lr: 0.001 loss: FocalLoss(gamma=2.0) sampler: WeightedRandom mixup_alpha:0.2 # 3× expansion n_train: 2,924 → aug 8,772 split: subject-aware subjects: train 1–13 / val 14–16
04
Analysis & Visualization 04_Analysis_and_Visualization.ipynb

Generates all evaluation artifacts: confusion matrices, per-class precision/recall/F1, training history, UMAP embedding projections, and backbone comparison table. The actual output plots are shown in the Results section.

05
Mock Video Evaluation 05_Mock_Video_Eval.ipynb

Runs inference on annotated MP4 videos with the full sliding-window pipeline: 32-frame buffer, inference every 16 frames, min_confidence=0.25. Produces per-person temporal strips — bridging academic eval to production-like behavior.

08
HITL Session Review 08_Session_Log_Review.ipynb

Human-in-the-Loop audit: review session crops, tracks, temporal strips, correct labels via a person registry. Feeds corrections back for next training round. Mirrors the /har-hitl UI in the production system.

Why Frozen Backbones?

Transfer learning efficiency: V-JEPA 2 and DINOv2 encode rich visual semantics learned from millions of samples — object parts, motion patterns, spatial relationships. These generalize to industrial environments without domain-specific fine-tuning.

Edge feasibility: Only the small MLP head (≈200K params) is updated and stored in the checkpoint. At inference, the backbone runs once per window; the MLP adds negligible latency on edge hardware.

Embedding Space Properties

DINOv2 [CLS] token: Encodes global scene semantics. Similar actions cluster in embedding space across subjects, lighting, and camera angles — shown by UMAP projections with action-class clusters.

V-JEPA 2 temporal context: Masked patch prediction enforces temporal consistency. The embedding captures motion dynamics — picking up vs. putting down, moving left vs. right — in a compact 1024-dim representation.

Experimental Results — Actual Notebook Outputs

All figures are direct outputs of 04_Analysis_and_Visualization.ipynb. No cherry-picking — exact pipeline artifacts from the InHARD validation set (n=501).

Fig 1a — DINOv2 · Class distribution. Training set imbalance: Picking left (641 clips) vs. Take subsystem (39 clips) = 16.4× ratio. Addressed by Focal Loss γ=2.0 + Weighted Sampler + MixUp 3×.
Fig 1b — DINOv2 · Confusion matrix on n=501 validation clips. Best performance on high-frequency actions. Challenges with rare classes (<77 clips).
Fig 1c — DINOv2 · Per-class Precision / Recall / F1. Classes with sufficient training samples achieve F1 > 0.5. Rare classes (Take measuring rod, Put down subsystem) show lower recall.
Fig 1d — DINOv2 · Training history over 100 epochs. Val loss converges to 1.015. Training uses 8,772 MixUp-augmented samples; validation uses original 501 clips.
Fig 2a — V-JEPA 2 · Class distribution. Same InHARD setup; 3,423 clips (2 fewer — corrupt clip skip). Subject-aware split mirrors DINOv2 for fair comparison.
Fig 2b — V-JEPA 2 · Confusion matrix on n=501 clips. Lower diagonal density than DINOv2 — temporal motion embeddings less discriminative for top-down industrial actions in this configuration.
Fig 2c — V-JEPA 2 · Per-class PRF1. Macro F1 = 0.321 vs DINOv2 0.425. Spatial arrangement differences (left vs. front picking) are less captured by temporal motion features.
Fig 2d — V-JEPA 2 · Training history. Best val loss = 1.370 vs DINOv2 1.015. More volatile convergence across 100 epochs — DINOv2 features are more linearly separable for this HAR task.

Interpretation

DINOv2's self-supervised spatial features provide more linearly separable representations for top-down industrial clips than V-JEPA 2's masked-prediction embeddings. For clips with a fixed top-down view, the rich spatial appearance of hand–object interactions is more discriminative than motion dynamics alone. The 8.8 pp accuracy gap is significant at n=501. Future work: partial V-JEPA 2 fine-tuning with industrial video pre-training may close the gap.

Key Findings & Conclusions

Academic contributions from this prototype cycle.

Finding 1
DINOv2 superiority for top-down industrial HAR

Frozen DINOv2 (ViT-L/14) outperforms V-JEPA 2 by 8.8 pp accuracy on InHARD 12-class top-down HAR. Spatial patch features from image SSL are more discriminative than temporal video masked prediction for this task geometry.

Finding 2
Transfer learning viability on industrial video

Pre-trained vision foundation models transfer effectively to industrial HAR without domain-specific pre-training — achieving 41.5% accuracy on a severely imbalanced 12-class problem with only a lightweight MLP head trained on ≈2,924 subject-disjoint clips.

Finding 3
Class imbalance is the dominant challenge

16.4× imbalance (641 vs. 39 clips). Combined mitigation — Focal Loss γ=2.0, Weighted Sampler, MixUp 3× — was necessary but insufficient for rare classes. Per-class F1 (Fig 1c) reveals this directly. Collecting more clips for rare classes is the highest-leverage intervention.

Finding 4
End-to-end system closes the Ver·Guiar·Mejorar loop

Full-stack integration (HAR → deviation detection → alert dispatch → timeline → HITL → analytics) demonstrates the complete Industria 4.0 feedback loop. Detection latency drops from 15+ min (manual) to <1 s (automated), with full audit trail.
